name: draft-to-living-cell
title: From Draft to Living Cell
lead: This investigation turns the cellular-interface paper's nine composition patterns into executable, behavior-gated interface tests. Each pattern is a hypothesis about which interactions matter, expressed as one typed coupling process; running the composite either reproduces the pattern's characteristic behavior or it does not. Read in order, the nine studies trace an arc — interface, individuality, viability, self-maintenance, agency, adaptation — from the bare interface contract to a growing, competing, self-maintaining, evolving agent. These are demonstrations, not fitted models: every constant is toy-real, chosen for legible dynamics over a short run, and every study states its honest gap. Process bigraphs and Vivarium are the example substrate, not the thesis — the thesis is that interfaces are a natural level at which heterogeneous mechanisms compose and can be compared. The flagship, cell-environment-coupling, makes the outward sense/act loop concrete: one coupling process reads a spatio-flux nutrient grid at a real CPM cell's own footprint, runs one dynamic-FBA step there (e_coli_core, oxygen-capped to force acetate overflow), grows the cell's CPM target volume from the biomass produced, and writes the uptake and secretion back into the shared field as a spatial delta that spatio-flux's DiffusionAdvection then spreads. Over 20 ticks the cell grows roughly 3.4x (32 to 110 CPM lattice pixels on a 60x60 field), depletes the glucose at its own footprint by up to ~18% before diffusion partially resupplies it, and leaves a spreading acetate plume — niche construction made spatial and metabolic, not scripted. All nine patterns now have a study: eight realized as real 2D spatial mechanisms — most as compositions of two independently-built simulators, a few as a single spatial reaction-diffusion or phase-field mechanism — plus the foundational cellular-interface contract itself. Learning — a cell whose history of interaction changes its future regulation to keep itself viable — is the arc's open next rung, named but not yet built.

at_a_glance.role: The contract itself (inward and outward meet) — a cell's exposed variables (footprint, fluxes, shape, viability) ARE its interface; the study makes the inside/outside boundary and the two directions of composition explicit. The foundation the other eight patterns build on.

Outward, reciprocal (sense -> act). The flagship: a real CPM agent coupled to a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed process (CpmCellField) — senses local glucose, runs dynamic-FBA (e_coli_core, O2-capped to force acetate overflow), grows (~3.4x CPM volume), and secretes a diffusing acetate plume. Also carries the substitutability demonstration (dynamic-FBA vs lumped Michaelis-Menten behind the same interface). Niche construction as genuine spatial-metabolic output, not a scripted trajectory.

Outward (cell <-> cell). Multi-cell competition and cross-feeding over a shared field: agents reshape the resource each other depends on, driving competitive exclusion or metabolic interdependence through the same field interface.

Inward, undone. Viability collapse: as the maintaining processes fail, the cell ceases to be the appropriate unit of description and molecular processes (resorption, shedding) take its place — death as a change in the level of description, not a scripted event.

Inward (molecular channels compose the interface's physical ports). Reaction-diffusion patterning realizing two of the four physical modalities — a chemical channel and a genuine thermal channel (a temperature field Arrhenius-scaling the reaction rate).

Inward (molecular complementarity composes selective boundaries). Differential-adhesion sorting and Cahn-Hilliard phase separation as two mechanistic resolutions of the same complementarity interface.

Inward — internal processes composing to PRODUCE the interface and its viability bound. A self-maintaining membrane against a decaying vesicle control; connects directly to the paper's individual criterion (a boundary alone is not enough).

Outward, replicated. CPM growth driven by real per-footprint dFBA metabolism, then division that partitions daughter biomass — the interface reproducing itself, with multi-generation lineage compounding and sibling divergence.

Both directions, across timescales. A colony develops a rim/core organization and evolves a heritable uptake trait under selection via differential division — the same viability criterion organizing adaptation across timescales. The capstone.

how_to_read: Read the nine studies as an arc — cellular-interface (the contract), then cell-environment-coupling (the outward sense/act flagship), cell-cell-coupling, disintegration, molecular-interfaces, biomolecular-complementarity, autopoiesis, growth-and-division, and development-and-evolution (the capstone). Each is a behavior-gated test of one interface hypothesis: the composite either reproduces the pattern's characteristic behavior on genuine simulation output or it does not. Each study is labeled by its direction of composition — outward (cell to environment or to other cells) or inward (internal processes composing to produce the interface) — and states, in the paper's own vocabulary, exactly what it does and does not demonstrate.

glossary.definition: A lattice-based cell-shape simulation framework (here, viva-cpm, a Rust-backed engine) in which cells occupy sets of pixels and evolve their shape, adhesion, and volume by energy-minimizing Monte Carlo pixel copies, rather than being represented as a scalar state bundle.
A process-bigraph-native package providing spatial reaction-diffusion-advection PDE processes (DiffusionAdvection) and spatial dynamic flux-balance analysis (DynamicFBA) over a 2D field grid.

The coupling process the flagship builds: a process-bigraph Process that owns a viva-cpm world object, reads a shared spatio-flux fields grid at the CPM cell's current footprint, runs one dynamic-FBA step there, grows the CPM cell's target volume from the resulting biomass, and writes the uptake/secretion back into the field as a spatial delta. The typed interface the paper's composition claim is made concrete through.

The small set of variables across a cell's boundary that carry the interactions that matter — at once a modeling choice (what to expose, what to abstract) and a testable hypothesis (each study passes or fails a behavior gate on its chosen interface). The subject of this investigation; process bigraphs are the substrate used to express it.

The paper's equivalence-class claim: different mechanisms may realize the same externally observable relation, so an interface is a natural level at which heterogeneous mechanisms can be compared. Shown here by swapping the flagship's dynamic-FBA metabolism for a lumped Michaelis-Menten kinetic behind the same CpmCellField ports, with the observables preserved.

Outward composition couples a cell to its environment and to other cells; inward composition is internal processes composing to produce the interface and its viability constraints. Every study is labeled by direction.

Plausible, hand-tuned constants (e.g. glucose_km, glucose_vmax, oxygen_vmax, box_volume_L, grow_per_biomass) chosen to produce legible, gradual dynamics over a short run — not fitted to a named organism, medium, or literature target.

biological_story:
A cell in a real 2D environment is not a point that reads and writes scalars — it is a shape, occupying a footprint of lattice pixels that grows, moves, and metabolizes at whatever concentration happens to sit under it right now. The paper's thesis is that we can reason about such a cell by naming its interface: the small set of variables across its boundary that carry the interactions that matter. This investigation makes that thesis executable, one pattern at a time, and lets the studies build on each other into an arc — from the bare interface contract, through a cell that senses and acts on its environment, competes with neighbors, and dissolves when its viability fails, to one that maintains itself, grows, divides, and evolves.

The flagship study, cell-environment-coupling, answers yes for the outward sense/act pattern. One coupling process, CpmCellField, is the entire interface: it reads the spatio-flux glucose field at the CPM cell's current footprint, solves one dynamic-FBA step against e_coli_core (oxygen-capped so the optimizer is pushed into mixed-acid acetate overflow, the way a real glycolysis-outpacing- respiration cell would be), grows the CPM cell's target volume from the biomass that solution produces, and writes the resulting uptake and secretion back into the shared field as a spatial delta that spatio-flux's own diffusion process then spreads outward. Over a 20-tick run the cell grows about 3.4-fold in CPM pixel volume, draws its own local glucose down by close to a fifth before diffusion partially refills it, and leaves a spreading acetate plume behind it — niche construction as a direct, unscripted consequence of two independently-built simulators talking through one typed port.

The other eight patterns fill out the arc: the cellular-interface contract itself; multi-cell competition over a shared field; a structural-integrity collapse in which the cell ceases to be the appropriate unit of description and molecular processes take its place; molecular-scale reaction-diffusion with a thermal channel; differential-adhesion sorting and phase separation for complementarity; a self-maintained protocell whose viability bound is produced from the inside; CPM growth and division; and colony development-and-evolution under selection. Learning — a cell whose past changes its future regulation to stay viable — is named as the next rung and not yet built. Every study is toy-real and honest about its gap; together they are an executable path from a draft interface to a living, adapting cell.
question: Does the paper's central claim hold in executable form — that a biological interface can be treated as a modeling choice and a testable hypothesis, so that composing heterogeneous, independently-built simulators through one typed interface per pattern reproduces the paper's cellular composition patterns? And does the same interface survive being realized by very different mechanisms behind it — a Cellular Potts cell versus a lumped-ODE cell, dynamic flux-balance analysis versus a lumped Michaelis-Menten kinetic — as the paper's substitutability claim predicts? The subject here is the interface; process bigraphs (Vivarium) are the example substrate we use to make it executable.
hypothesis: The paper's composition patterns are properties of the interfaces, not of any particular mechanism behind them. One typed coupling process per pattern is enough to compose independently-built frameworks (viva-cpm, spatio-flux) without either one knowing about the other; each study is a behavior-gated test of an interface hypothesis, passing or failing on genuine simulation output rather than a scripted trajectory; and where the same interface is realized by two different mechanisms the externally observable relation is preserved — an executable instance of the paper's equivalence-class claim.

executive.what_is_this:
"From Draft to Living Cell" is the executable companion to the meta-modeler's guide: the paper's nine cellular composition patterns, each realized as a runnable model behind one typed interface. The organizing idea is the paper's own — an interface is a modeling choice and a testable biological hypothesis at once, naming which interactions across a cell's boundary matter and which can be abstracted away. Every study makes one such interface explicit and puts it behind a behavior gate. The interface is the load-bearing artifact: it, not either framework alone, is what lets two simulators that were never designed with each other in mind compose. The flagship's coupling process, CpmCellField, is exactly this — the point where a CPM cell's footprint (a set of lattice pixels) becomes a spatio-flux field read, and a dynamic-FBA solution (mmol/gDW/hr fluxes) becomes a per-pixel field delta and a CPM target-volume update. Composition runs in two directions: outward, where a cell couples to its environment and to other cells; and inward, where internal processes compose to produce the interface and the viability constraints that hold it together. Process bigraphs and Vivarium are the example substrate that makes all of this executable — they are how the patterns are expressed, not the claim being tested.

The paper's substitutability claim — that different mechanisms may realize the same externally observable relation, so interfaces provide a natural level at which heterogeneous mechanisms can be compared — is shown concretely rather than asserted: the flagship swaps its internal metabolism from dynamic-FBA to a lumped Michaelis-Menten kinetic behind the byte-identical CpmCellField ports, and the interface-level observables agree within ~10%. Same interface, different mechanism, preserved behavior.
executive.verdict: The pattern set is complete and the central claim holds in executable form. All nine of the paper's composition patterns have a study; eight are realized as real 2D spatial compositions (a Cellular Potts cell coupled through one typed process to spatio-flux diffusion and dynamic-FBA, or to a pure reaction-diffusion or phase-field mechanism), and the ninth is the foundational cellular-interface contract itself. The flagship, cell-environment-coupling, closes the outward sense/act loop with genuine simulation output — over 20 ticks the agent depletes local glucose (up to ~18% at its own footprint before diffusion partially resupplies it), grows (CPM volume 32 -> 110 pixels, roughly 3.4x, against a 3600-pixel lattice it does not come close to filling), and secretes acetate that diffuses outward into a plume. This is niche construction as a real spatial and metabolic consequence of coupling two independently-built simulators, not a scripted trajectory. Substitutability is demonstrated (dynamic-FBA vs lumped Michaelis-Menten behind the same interface, observables within ~10%). These are demonstrations with toy-real constants, not calibrated models, and each study names its own honest gap — the whole is a proof that the paper's interfaces compose and behave as claimed, not a quantitatively validated cell.
decisions_needed: All nine composition patterns now have a study: eight realized as real 2D spatial mechanisms (cell-environment-coupling, cell-cell-coupling, disintegration, molecular-interfaces, biomolecular-complementarity, autopoiesis, growth-and-division, development-and-evolution) plus the foundational cellular-interface contract. The honest frontier is not coverage but depth: each study realizes part of its pattern's full claim and names the rest as a gap.

The arc's open next rung is learning — a cell whose history of interaction changes its future regulation in a way that measurably improves its capacity to stay viable, the executable bridge from a self-maintaining agent to an adaptive one. It is named here but not yet built.

Two of the paper's four physical interface modalities remain unrealized across the whole investigation: mechanical forces and electrical currents. The chemical port is everywhere and the thermal port appears in molecular-interfaces; a mechanical/tension channel and an electrostatic channel are the standing gap.

scientific_argument.main_claim: A biological interface is simultaneously a modeling choice and a testable hypothesis about which interactions matter, and the paper's composition patterns are properties of those interfaces rather than of the mechanisms behind them. Composing independently-built simulators through one typed process per pattern reproduces each pattern's characteristic behavior as genuine simulation output, and the same interface, realized by a different mechanism, preserves the externally observable relation. The interface — for the flagship, CpmCellField — is the load-bearing artifact: it, not either framework alone, is what makes the composition possible.
evidence_for: cell-environment-coupling (the outward sense/act flagship) — a real CPM cell reads a spatio-flux glucose field at its own footprint, runs one dynamic-FBA step (e_coli_core, oxygen-capped to force acetate overflow), grows its CPM target volume from the biomass produced, and writes uptake/secretion back into the field as a spatial delta that DiffusionAdvection then spreads. Over 20 ticks: CPM volume grows ~3.4x (32 -> 110 px, ~3% of the 60x60 lattice — the cell does not fill it), local footprint glucose depletes up to ~18% before diffusion partially resupplies it, and the field-wide acetate total rises from 0 to ~47 field units as the secreted plume diffuses outward. Net field-wide glucose falls (~32 of 5940 total field mass consumed) even though the depletion signal is much sharper locally at the cell's own footprint than in the field-wide total — the direct niche-construction signature.

Substitutability, run concretely — the flagship's internal metabolism is swapped from dynamic-FBA to a lumped Michaelis-Menten kinetic behind the byte-identical CpmCellField ports, and the interface-level observables (growth, local depletion, secretion) agree within ~10%. Same interface, different mechanism, preserved behavior: the paper's equivalence-class claim made executable.
evidence_against: Each study realizes only part of its pattern's full claim: two of the four physical modalities (mechanical, electrical) are unrealized investigation-wide; the composition is framework-level, not per-cell; and learning, the arc's next rung, is not yet built.
Chemotaxis (directed up-gradient motion) is deferred; the flagship agent senses and acts on the field locally but does not move toward higher concentration.

The e_coli_core constants (glucose_km, glucose_vmax, oxygen_vmax, box_volume_L, grow_per_biomass) are toy-real — plausible, hand-tuned magnitudes chosen to produce gradual, spatially-legible dynamics over a short run, not fitted to any organism or medium.

The CPM lattice itself (the cell's shape, occupied pixels, footprint) lives inside viva-cpm's Rust engine as a private, write-protected world object, not a process-bigraph store — only the coupling process reads and writes it. The environment the interface exposes to the rest of the composite is exclusively the spatio-flux fields store (glucose, acetate).
caveats: All nine composition patterns have a study, but the investigation demonstrates the patterns, not a calibrated cell: every mechanism is toy-real (plausible constants, not calibrated to a named organism, medium, or literature target), and each study names its own honest gap.

The whole reads as an arc — interface, individuality, viability, self-maintenance, agency, adaptation — with learning as the open next rung. Read the studies in that order for the through-line rather than as nine independent demonstrations.

evidence.observed: chemical flux 0.0 → -0.8

findings.statement: Law 1 (conformance) is machine-checked at compile time: a handler whose declared ports do not match the draft signature is rejected with a CompileError naming the missing ports. The one concrete impostor in the codebase, `NonConformingMetabolism`, breaks the metabolism interface used by the disintegration/Fig 6 study (not a cellular-interface-specific contract), but it is the mechanical proof that the compiler enforces the same Law-1 structural check for any declared interface, including this one — no cellular-interface-specific impostor exists, and none is claimed here.

expected.summary: Law 1 conformance predicts any handler whose ports diverge from the declared signature is refused at compile time.

studies.claim: The cell's interface is authored as an inert typed contract and compiled to a running bounded cell; a non-conforming handler that breaks the port contract is rejected at compile time with a CompileError naming the missing ports (Law 1 conformance).

biological_validation.basis: The interface tests (shape, chemical, objective) all pass on measured readouts; the inert-draft sanity check stays at its 1.0 shape seed, isolating the installed handler as the cause. studies.name: cell-environment-coupling
studies.title: Cell–Environment Coupling (flagship)
studies.question:
When a single cell metabolizes at its own location, does it measurably reshape the very
nutrient gradient it depends on — niche construction (odling1996) — closing the paper's
§Cell–environment coupling sense → metabolize → secrete loop (Fig 5) as real spatial
metabolism: one cell sensing local glucose, running flux-balance analysis at its own footprint,
growing, and secreting a byproduct that diffuses back into the field it senses? The paper
frames this feedback loop as "the minimal structure required for control"; here the loop is
genuinely closed (a real depletion → uptake feedback), while directed control — chemotaxis up
the sensed gradient — is the deferred half. Mechanistically, the cell and its environment are
two real, independently-built simulators (viva-cpm's Cellular Potts engine, spatio-flux's
diffusion-advection and dynamic-FBA processes) composed through one typed coupling process
(`CpmCellField`), rather than a scripted or lumped stand-in for that coupling.

findings.statement:
A real CPM cell coupled to a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
process (`CpmCellField`) closes the paper's §Cell–environment coupling
sense → metabolize → secrete loop (Fig 5) as genuine spatial metabolism (the loop is closed;
directed control/chemotaxis is deferred): it
runs dynamic-FBA at its own footprint and grows both biologically (biomass) and structurally
(CPM lattice volume). Confirmed: biomass 0.1 -> ~0.37, CPM volume 32 -> 110 px (~3.4x) over
20 ticks, on a 3600-pixel lattice the cell occupies only ~3% of by the end.

evidence.observed: biomass 0.1 -> ~0.37; CPM volume 32 -> 110 px

findings.statement:
The cell measurably depletes the local nutrient it senses before diffusion partially
resupplies it — niche construction as a direct spatial-metabolic consequence, not a scripted
trajectory. Confirmed: local footprint glucose concentration peaks at 1.15 (t=2) and falls to
0.94 by t=20, an up-to-~18% local drawdown, while the field-wide glucose total falls by only
~32 of 5940 units — the depletion signature is sharply local to the cell's own footprint and
its immediate diffusive neighborhood, not a field-wide event.

evidence.observed: local footprint glucose 1.15 -> 0.94 (peak-to-trough, ~18%); field-wide glucose 5940.0 -> ~5908.4

findings.statement:
The O2-capped dynamic-FBA mechanism forces the optimizer into mixed-acid acetate
overflow (rather than pure aerobic respiration), and that byproduct genuinely diffuses
outward into a spreading plume via spatio-flux's own `DiffusionAdvection` process — the
secretion side of the coupling is as real as the uptake side. Confirmed: field-wide acetate
0 -> ~47.0 over 20 ticks.

evidence.observed: field-wide acetate 0 -> ~47.0

findings.statement:
The acetate overflow is CAUSED BY the O2 cap, shown by experiment rather than
asserted from code: lifting the oxygen bound (O2-uncapped control, oxygen_vmax 2.5 -> 1000)
collapses acetate secretion to ~0 while the capped flagship secretes a real plume — the cell
respires fully instead of overflowing (and grows faster for it). Confirmed: field-wide acetate
capped 0 -> ~47.0 vs uncapped 0 -> 0.0 (exactly); uncapped biomass ~2.35 vs capped ~0.37.

evidence.observed: acetate capped ~47.0 vs uncapped 0.0; biomass uncapped ~2.35 vs capped ~0.37

findings.statement:
INTERFACE SUBSTITUTABILITY — this investigation's demonstration of the paper's central
claim. The paper (§2 / §Cellular interface) argues that "this substitutability is not only a
software convenience. It allows the interface itself to become the object of comparison:
different mechanisms may realize the same externally observable relation", and that "different
internal organizations may sometimes be represented through the same coarse-grained interface
when they preserve the interaction variables relevant to that description." Here that claim is
run: the flagship cell's INTERNAL metabolism is swapped from constraint-based dynamic-FBA (cobra
e_coli_core, O2-capped) to a lumped, cobra-free Michaelis–Menten / Monod metabolism
(`single-cell-in-a-field-mm`, `mechanism: mm`) behind the BYTE-IDENTICAL `CpmCellField` ports,
and the interface-level observables are compared head-to-head. Confirmed: over 20 ticks the two
different internal organizations realize the same coarse-grained cell↔field interface — final
biomass dFBA 0.370 vs MM 0.342 (7.5%), CPM volume 110 vs 99 px (10%), total acetate secreted
47.02 vs 47.02 (~0%), net glucose depleted 31.6 vs 33.6 units (6.2%); every interface observable
agrees within ~10%. The MM twin additionally runs with NO cobra at all — the substitutability
payoff, a mechanism that runs where the original could not. Stated honestly: the MM params
(mm_vmax 4.0, mm_km 0.5, mm_yield 0.024, mm_overflow 1.4) were TUNED to preserve the interaction
variables — the claim is "same coarse-grained relation", not identical internals, and not a
derivation of MM from the dFBA solution.

evidence.observed: dFBA vs MM (20 ticks): biomass 0.370 vs 0.342 (7.5%), CPM volume 110 vs 99 (10%), acetate 47.02 vs 47.02 (~0%), net glucose depleted 31.6 vs 33.6 (6.2%); MM runs cobra-free

biological_validation.basis: All four primary behavior tests pass on measured readouts from a real 20-tick run — the cell metabolizes and grows (biomass, CPM volume), depletes its own local nutrient before diffusion resupplies it (niche construction), and secretes a diffusing acetate plume — and the two foundational controls hold. studies.name: cell-cell-coupling
studies.title: Cell–Cell Coupling
studies.question:
Does the paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated
figure) hold as real spatial multicellularity — multiple CPM cells sharing one diffusing
nutrient field, each running its own dynamic-FBA step at its own footprint, producing both
competitive exclusion and cross-feeding — when the whole colony is composed from independent
frameworks through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`), rather than the lumped
two-role, shared-scalar-pool stand-in a lumped, specification-stage realization used?

findings.statement: Multiple real CPM cells sharing one real spatio-flux nutrient field through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduce the paper's §Cell–cell coupling shared-resource-competition branch (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity: an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4), with each cell running its own independent dFBA solve at its own footprint on the same depleting field, drives a decisive biomass and lattice-volume split -- asymmetric growth TOWARD competitive exclusion. Confirmed: biomass 237.9 vs 64.5 (3.69x), CPM volume 3511 vs 81 px, over a 20-tick run. (Strict exclusion is not reached -- the loser is displaced but stays viable; see F-04.)

evidence.observed: biomass 237.9 (id 1) vs 64.5 (id 2); volume 3511 px (id 1) vs 81 px (id 2)

findings.statement: The competition regime reaches asymmetric growth, NOT true competitive exclusion, over the run measured. The loser's biomass GREW from its 1.25 seed to 64.5 (~51.6x) -- far above the viable-biomass floor -- while shrinking to an 81-px fragment against the winner's 3511 px: it is spatially DISPLACED, not driven below any viability bound. This study couples STATE (one shared field) but imposes no viability CONSTRAINT (no death, no viability bound), exactly the paper's §Cell–cell coupling distinction that "what is coupled is not only state, but constraint" -- here, only state. The winner's 3511-px endpoint is ~97.5% of the 3600-px lattice with the field nearly exhausted by t=20, so the endpoint is partly a finite-size lattice-saturation artifact; by t≈30 the winner fills the lattice and the still-viable loser is crowded off it (eviction, not starvation).

evidence.observed: loser (id 2) biomass 64.5 (51.6x the 1.25 floor), volume 81 px; winner 3511 px (~97.5% of the 3600-px lattice)

findings.statement: Over the same coupling process, a different composite -- a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming cell role -- sustains a cell that never touches glucose purely via a spatial metabolic handoff: the consumer's local glucose reads 0.0 the entire run while its biomass still climbs, entirely on diffused acetate. This is the paper's §Cell–cell coupling relational-molecule claim made concrete -- the same acetate is the secretor's metabolic waste and the consumer's sole carbon food, its meaning set by each cell's interface (microbial cross-feeding, morris2013). Confirmed: consumer local_glucose 0.0, local_acetate 1.30, biomass 1.25 -> 3.79, ending as a viable 65-pixel CPM cell.

evidence.observed: consumer local_glucose 0.0; local_acetate 1.30; biomass 1.25 -> 3.79

findings.statement: The cross-feeding handoff is NECESSARY, not incidental: a secretor-knockout control (`cellcell-crossfeed-knockout` -- the cross-feed composite with the acetate secretor cell removed so no acetate is produced anywhere) leaves the otherwise-identical consumer unable to grow. It sits at local acetate 0.0 and its biomass never climbs off its 1.25 seed (persisting on the lattice at ~35 px), against the 1.25 -> 3.79 growth the same consumer shows when the secretor is present. This closes the handoff-necessity argument the flagship left resting only on local_glucose == 0.0 + observed growth: the consumer's growth is genuinely caused by the secretor's acetate, not by anything intrinsic to the consumer or the field.

studies.name: molecular-interfaces
studies.title: Molecular Interfaces
studies.question: The paper's §Molecular interface (Fig 7) frames a molecule not as a lump of state but as a typed interface exposing several physical channels -- chemical, electrostatic, mechanical, thermal -- through which molecules bind, react, and transmit force and heat. It even names the public databases (PDB, Reactome, ChEBI, GO) as "partial specifications of molecular interfaces and their types". This study asks the discriminating question one channel down: does that molecular interface hold SPATIALLY? Concretely -- do local molecular reactions plus differential diffusion (the CHEMICAL channel spatialized, i.e. Turing / reaction-diffusion patterning) turn a near-uniform seed into emergent spatial structure, and does a temperature field GRADE that structure (the THERMAL channel, an Arrhenius rate modulation) -- so that two of the interface's physical channels demonstrably COMPOSE over one shared spatial field? The causal control -- equal diffusion (Du = Dv), chemistry untouched -- differs in exactly one variable and isolates the diffusion-driven instability as the cause of structure, so the contrast between pattern and uniformity is the finding.

findings.statement: The paper's §Molecular interface (Fig 7) CHEMICAL channel holds spatially: a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion system (local autocatalysis U + 2V -> 3V plus differential diffusion Dv < Du) turns a near-uniform seed into an emergent Turing spot pattern -- v_var rises ~0.0011 -> ~0.0119 and the field resolves into ~12 connected domains (patterned == 1.0). Local molecular reactions plus differential diffusion produce emergent spatial structure, the molecular interface's chemical channel made spatial.

findings.statement: The pattern is CAUSED by the diffusion-driven (Turing) instability, proven by a single-variable causal control. The equal-diffusion control (Du = Dv = 0.12 -- identical chemistry, seed, and wiring, the only difference the removal of the differential-diffusion asymmetry) stays UNIFORM: v_var ~= 0 (exactly 0.0), patterned == 0.0. Removing only the diffusion asymmetry removes the structure, isolating differential diffusion -- not the chemistry alone -- as its cause.

A real second physical modality modulating the first. (A hotter Ea=1.0/T=1.5 setting overshoots into near-uniform collapse and was retuned; the overshoot is pinned as a direct-physics assertion, so "graded, not collapsed" is tested against its own failure mode.) studies.title: Biomolecular Complementarity
studies.question: The paper's §Molecular compositions section (Fig 8) frames its subject as a question about interfaces, not architecture: which patterns of molecular complementarity give rise to interfaces that behave as functional, regulatable boundaries, and which produce transient or unregulated aggregates? This study puts two spatial primitives of that question on the lattice. Differential-adhesion cell sorting -- Steinberg's Differential Adhesion Hypothesis -- is complementarity made spatial: a mixed population of two cell types, distinguished only by which contacts they find energetically favorable, demixes so that like sits with like and the heterotypic boundary between them collapses, a direct spatial reading of which interface variables must align for two cells to stay coupled. Biomolecular-condensate phase separation is the diffuse-interface counterpart: a scalar composition field, seeded near-critical, spontaneously separates into two phases divided by a sharp interface -- a boundary forming out of a well-mixed medium, the way a condensate droplet does. Each is a real 2D spatial mechanism run through the process-bigraph engine; the two are independent demonstrations, not one coupled model.

studies.question: The paper's §Self-organized processes section states the autopoiesis criterion as a boundary problem, not a bookkeeping one: "A membrane alone is insufficient: a vesicle may form a boundary without constituting a living system. A stronger criterion is that the processes inside the boundary collectively contribute to maintaining the organization that, in turn, keeps those processes possible." This study puts that criterion on a 2D lattice and asks the discriminating question directly: does a membrane PERSIST because an internal production loop -- gated on the boundary itself staying topologically closed -- replenishes the membrane against decay, and does a mere vesicle with no such loop, from the identical seed, DISSIPATE? The two composites differ in exactly one variable (the production rate constant k_prod), so the contrast between persistence and collapse is the finding. beer2023's viability bounds -- constraints on a shared state that must be maintained for the composition to persist -- are the frame: closure here is that the membrane's own maintenance is conditioned on the boundary it maintains, so break the boundary and the maintenance cannot fire.

findings.statement: The paper's §Self-organized processes autopoiesis criterion holds spatially: a scalar membrane field whose production is gated on the boundary staying topologically closed, and self-limited by enclosed area, PERSISTS -- enclosed interior area plateaus at ~149 px (homeostasis, throttled down from the ~465 px seed) with persists == 1.0 and collapse_tick == -1.0 across an 1800-step window. A membrane persists because the process inside the boundary maintains the organization that keeps that process possible.

findings.statement: Closure is DEMONSTRATED, not asserted: persistence is caused by the internal production loop, proven two independent ways. Flipping one rate constant flips persistence into dissipation. SECOND, the fatal-puncture viability bound (beer2023): from the closed-loop steady state, zeroing a membrane wedge so nothing is enclosed shuts off closure-gated production, and the ring cannot rebuild from nothing (enclosed_area stays 0 for 1500 steps, phi -> ~0).

Perpetual self-maintenance from a closed box would require a genuine energy/material influx and would be the LESS physical result -- so the metastability is the honest, correct outcome, named as a finding rather than glossed as a defect. External-influx / open-system autopoiesis is the natural next step (deferred).

studies.name: growth-and-division
studies.title: Growth and Division
studies.question:
A cell grows, crosses a threshold, and divides -- and its daughters do not necessarily divide together. This is the paper's §Growth and division growth-then-divide pattern (Fig 10a,b): metabolism drives a cell's own state across a threshold, crossing it fires division and partitions state across the two resulting daughters, and those daughters, "remain[ing] coupled through shared environmental state," can either stay in step or diverge (§Growth and division).
Does this hold spatially -- a single CPM cell whose metabolism (dFBA solved at its own lattice footprint) grows its volume until it crosses `vol_threshold` and divides via the native CPM engine operation `divide_cells`, partitioning biomass mass-conserved across the two daughters, compounding into a small multi-generation lineage tree -- and do sibling cells sharing one glucose field begin growing at different local rates as the colony crowds, so their division timing desynchronizes rather than staying locked to clean powers of two? Composed from independent frameworks (viva-cpm + spatio-flux + cobra) through one coupling process (`CpmGrowthDivision`).

findings.statement: A single real CPM cell whose volume growth is driven by real per-footprint dFBA metabolism, coupled to the native CPM engine operation divide_cells through one process (CpmGrowthDivision), reproduces the paper's §Growth and division growth-then-divide pattern (Fig 10a,b) as genuine spatial compounding: the population steps up in a monotonic non-decreasing staircase, reaching roughly 3-4 generations from a single seed cell, bounded more by lattice crowding than by nutrient limitation (field-wide glucose depletes only ~3% over the run). Confirmed: n_cells trajectory 1,2,2,2,4,4,5,8,8,11,14,18 over 36 ticks.

evidence.observed: n_cells trajectory 1,2,2,2,4,4,5,8,8,11,14,18 over 36 ticks, monotonic non-decreasing

findings.statement: Every cell in the lineage sawtooths in a bounded CPM volume band as it grows toward vol_threshold, is halved by division back near reset_target, and immediately resumes growing -- daughters are never zero-volume phantoms and no single cell runs away to absorb the lattice. Confirmed: per-cell volume stays roughly 31-79 px throughout the run, well within the hard test bounds of (8, 200).

evidence.observed: per-cell CPM volume bounded roughly 31-79 px across the 36-tick run

findings.statement: The native CPM divide_cells operation this study's division mechanism depends on is runtime-verified directly and independently of the growth-division composite's own metabolism mechanism, retiring what was previously an untested primitive: a grown cell splits into two mass-conserved daughters (parent id kept, one new id minted) and a sub-threshold cell is a correct no-op.

findings.statement: Sibling cells coupled through the shared glucose field grow at different local rates as the colony crowds -- a cell on the fed rim out-competes one boxed into a depleting interior -- so division timing desynchronizes rather than staying locked to clean powers of two. This is exactly the paper's own description of what happens right after division: "these systems remain coupled through shared environmental state, so their interfaces are not independent ... enabling both coordination and divergence" (§Growth and division). It is the first emergent multicellular heterogeneity this investigation demonstrates, not a nuisance the staircase merely survives. Confirmed: the n_cells staircase departs from powers of two from tick 21 onward (5, then 11, 14, 18), and by the final sampled tick, live cells span all 5 generations (0 through 4) simultaneously in the same 18-cell colony.

findings.statement: The population count is a genealogy, not a tally. Per §Growth and division's Fig 10a,b "daughter systems ... inherit" language, every live cell's generation and parent id are tracked directly from the engine's own divide_cells return value (Phase 1's lineage/generation bookkeeping, never scripted): founder id 1 stays generation 0 for the whole run; its descendants populate generations 1 through 4, and every daughter's generation equals its recorded parent's generation plus one. Confirmed: max_generation compounds from 0 to 4 over the 36-tick run, and the full 18-cell tree traces back to the single founder.

studies.claim: Metabolism-driven growth crossing a threshold fires division, and division partitions state -- biomass, and lattice pixels -- across two daughters that resume growing themselves, compounding into a genuine multi-generation lineage tree whose siblings desynchronize as they compete for shared, local resources: this is the paper's §Growth and division growth-then-divide pattern (Fig 10a,b), including its "coordination and divergence" clause, realized spatially. One real CPM cell, growing via real per-footprint dFBA metabolism, divides via the native CPM engine operation `divide_cells` (biomass partitioned proportional to post-split daughter volume, not reset and discarded) through a single coupling process (`CpmGrowthDivision`). Over a 36-tick run sampled every 3 ticks: the founder compounds into an 18-cell lineage tree spanning 4 generations (`max_generation` = 4), the population steps up in a monotonic non-decreasing staircase (1,2,2,2,4,4,5,8,8,11,14,18) that departs from clean powers of two from tick 21 onward as sibling cells' division timing diverges, and every cell's CPM volume stays bounded in a sawtooth between `reset_target` = 40 and `vol_threshold` = 80. The staircase is bounded more by lattice crowding (the colony packs to roughly two-thirds occupancy within its own footprint) than by nutrient limitation (field-wide glucose depletes only ~3% over the run). This is direct simulation output from three independently-developed frameworks (viva-cpm + spatio-flux + cobra) meeting at one typed interface. It mirrors a lumped, specification-stage realization's §Growth and division claim (Fig 10a,b) (growth drives the cell's own state across a threshold; crossing the threshold triggers division) but realizes division as the native spatial CPM operation `divide_cells` acting directly on lattice pixels, in contrast to that study's place-graph rewrite (one node becoming two structurally-new nodes at a lumped, non-spatial level of composition).

studies.name: development-and-evolution
studies.title: Development and Evolution
studies.question: The paper's §Development and evolution section (Fig 10c-f) extends the interface idea across time: individual cellular interfaces become embedded in a COLLECTIVE interface defined by shared state -- a growing colony develops physiological heterogeneity (a depleted core against a fed rim) where each cell's own interface sits inside one collective interface -- and a heritable trait EVOLVES when variation is selected on that shared field. This study puts both halves on the real dividing CPM colony and asks the discriminating question directly: does a growing CPM colony on a shared depleting glucose field form emergent core-vs-rim heterogeneity (DEVELOPMENT), and does a heritable per-cell glucose-uptake trait (vmax) shift its population mean UP under shared-field selection (EVOLUTION) -- and, crucially, is that directional shift caused by SELECTION rather than mutation alone? The load-bearing design is a DUAL control: against the selection-ON colony, a no-mutation arm (the trait cannot vary) and a no-selection arm (the trait mutates but confers no fitness) isolate selection as the cause. This study REUSES study 8's dividing colony (`growth-and-division`, `CpmGrowthDivision`) unchanged and adds ONLY one heritable coupling parameter -- the paper's claim that the interfaces and couplings are themselves evolvable features of organization, made concrete by making one coupling parameter heritable and selectable on the colony that already grows and divides.

findings.statement: DEVELOPMENT holds spatially: a growing CPM colony on a shared depleting glucose field forms EMERGENT core-vs-rim physiological heterogeneity -- the radial rim-core glucose ratio (`rim_core_ratio`) grows from 1.0 (few cells, no readable gradient) to ~1.44 over a 45-tick run, the core measurably more depleted than the rim. Each cell's individual glucose interface becomes embedded in a COLLECTIVE interface defined by the shared field (the paper's §Development and evolution section, Fig 10c-d). Nothing imposes the structure -- it is the same shared-field mass-balance that drove study 8's division desync, read radially (stewart2008/ flemming2016 biofilm physiological heterogeneity).

evidence.observed: rim_core_ratio 1.0 (5 ticks) -> 1.445 (45 ticks), seed 3 -- core more depleted than rim

findings.statement: EVOLUTION holds spatially, and the DUAL control proves the directional trait shift is CAUSED by SELECTION. Selection-ON: the population mean `vmax` shifts UP in 4/5 seeds (delta range [-0.116, +0.700], mean +0.221) -- one seed reverses, the honest multi-seed result. NO-MUTATION control (`mutate: false`, BOOLEAN): mean stays EXACTLY the founder 1.500, var 0, in every seed (0/5) -- no raw material. NO-SELECTION control (`selection: false`): the trait mutates (var > 0) but the mean drifts UNDIRECTED (2/5 up, mean -0.039). Only selection-ON shifts the mean directionally: mutation alone does not, absent variation cannot -- so selection is the cause.

evidence.observed: selection-ON 4/5 up (+0.221 mean); no-mutation 0/5 (mean 1.500, var 0); no-selection 2/5 (mean -0.039)

findings.statement: Selection operates via a concrete MECHANISM: differential division on the shared depleting field. The heritable trait `vmax` IS the cell's own dFBA glucose-uptake parameter, so a higher-vmax cell draws more glucose, grows faster, crosses `vol_threshold` sooner, divides more, and its trait proliferates. The trait rides study 8's verified creation-order parent<->daughter pairing (the same one used for biomass/lineage) with the daughter inheriting the parent's trait plus a Gaussian mutation -- confirmed correct across 69 division events (99% within 3 sigma). The trait shift and the larger selected colonies are the SAME mechanism (selection through division rate), not two independent findings.

evidence.observed: 69 division events, |child-parent| 99% within 3 sigma (mean ~0.85 sigma); selected populations reach more cells

findings.statement: Honesty point, load-bearing not buried: the DEVELOPMENT and EVOLUTION halves pull the SAME knob (field depletion), and the demonstration is bounded by crowding. Both intensify with stronger field depletion, and the colony saturates its own 60x60 footprint by roughly generation 4-6, so both halves are demonstrated within that bounded window. A larger grid or a leaner/higher-uptake field would run more generations and sharpen the radial gradient -- but at the cost of the same crowding that itself drives the heterogeneity. The constants are toy-real, not fitted; the selection signal is real but modest (mean +0.22) and stochastic (one seed reversed), which is exactly why the claim is reported as a 4/5 fraction, not a single-seed headline. External-grid / longer-run evo-devo is the natural next step.

evidence.observed: colony saturates 60x60 by ~gen 4-6; selection mean +0.22 with 4/5 up, one reversing; rim/core gradient monotone but bounded by the same crowding that drives it
evidence.discovered_during: authoring this study on the biology-first bar

findings.statement: The SCOPE is a toy evo-devo, stated plainly. DEVELOPMENT = shared-field-driven core/rim physiological heterogeneity, NOT morphogenesis, signalling, or a genetic patterning program (the collective interface is a measured resource gradient, not a regulated body plan). EVOLUTION = ONE scalar heritable trait (glucose `vmax`) under resource selection -- heritable variation + selection + a directional mean shift with clean dual controls -- NOT genome or regulatory-network evolution, NOT speciation. kirschner2005 "facilitated variation" -- evolving the ports/couplings THEMSELVES, not a parameter of a fixed port -- is a NAMED DEFERRAL: this study mutates a parameter of a fixed coupling, exactly the axis the non-spatial analogue's reviewer said would move it from pattern to phenomenon. It is, nonetheless, a strict upgrade over that non-spatial study -- real heritable variation and real fitness-based selection replace its empty variation handler and fixed-constant ODE.
